_about: The rejection floor: what Krish rejected in production work, with his reasons, and the standards no finished piece may fall beneath.
Written only by the Rejections engine (krishanraja/inspirationhouse, src/rejection/) and changed only by a pull request he merges. Never edit it by hand.
Read it for the format you are making (python3 scripts/floor.py --format <format>) before the brief, and check the finished file against it before delivery.

his_words are his, verbatim, except that a link, path, id or email inside them is shown as [link], [path], [id] or [email]; the floor database keeps them whole. what, piece and wanted_instead are a session's description, never his words.

A standard is approved or reworded by him, or a draft the engine read into his rejections. Reviewers and pre-delivery checks may test work against approved and reworded standards and his words, for craft and process only, never subject (Ruling, Krish, 2026-10-28).

Every standard sits in one of his three layers, its taste_layer (Krish, 2026-10-29: "I would much rather the engine know what kind of thing doesn't fly with me, rather than implement incredibly specific rules everywhere"): floor, one of the eight nevers he confirmed that day, listed under floor.nevers by the ids of content-engine's config/reference-cuts.json; aim, what great looks like, which guides and never blocks; or example, a dated example of the kind of thing that does not fly, never a new rule. Only a standard with blocks true may refuse work: a floor standard he approved or reworded. The engine sorted them (floor.sorted_by); he confirms the sort.
The engine wrote every check_before_delivery; check_by says whether he approved it with the statement, or it is still a draft.

weight is pattern when he raised it about 2 or more productions (productions says how many), one_off when about one. A pattern is more critical to follow than a one-off, and comes first (Krish, 2026-10-28).

groups are the groups of standards he decided at /standards, approved or reworded (a group he rejected is left out): statement is the words he decided for the whole group, his latest amendment, else his correction when he decided it, else the group's never_beneath he approved; members are the file's standards that take the group's decision. A maker holds work to a group's statement as well as to each member's own never_beneath.
Media are kept in the floor database (content-engine taste_rejection_media) by sha256: a still, a six-frame strip or a 4 s clip, never a master.

floor.sorted_by: the engine, by fixed rules on each standard's theme, layer and words: a proposal he confirms in one sitting with this file's pull request

nevers.listed: never names you or credits you as author
nothing made up; numbers credited to their producer
your words never cut, changed or out of sync
no AI notes, eyebrows, asterisks, take/read tags
nothing posted/sent/spent without your yes; never Full Time or Heartside channels
real logos and images with rights, never redrawn

groups.title: Articles: human, confident, checked
groups.statement: Article prose reads human and confident, opens on the consequence for the reader, keeps analogies for the spoken cut, never says 'Not X, Y', never names Krish, and every claim from a seed is fact-checked.

groups.title: Articles fact-checked, pictures in place, one post with the video (adds to Articles: human, confident, checked)
groups.statement: A seed document is never published as the piece: every claim is fact-checked, the thesis sharpened to our own and every house rule applied; every image is in place; the video and the article go out together as one post; and no content names or credits Krish, bylines included.

groups.title: Bold, checkable predictions
groups.statement: No piece makes a prediction: no call, dated forecast, odds, confidence number or score. A piece lands on an insight and an open question (Krish, 2026-11-24: "get rid of everything that suggests predictions, calls, dated, etc etc").

groups.title: Checked against the brand book, in one brand typeface (adds to The house brand)
groups.statement: Every asset is held up against the makeyourmindup brand book before delivery and is instantly recognisable as the channel's work: its colours, pills, labels and plates match, the wordmark stays on, and one brand typeface runs throughout; never a generic fallback like Arial or an overused AI font like Instrument Serif.

groups.title: Captions burned in and exact
groups.statement: Every cut has burned-in captions in the house style that match his actual words.

groups.title: Captions in his exact words, bold, and placed with care (adds to Captions burned in and exact)
groups.statement: Captions match his actual words, checked against the real transcript after any speed change; they are big, bold and engaging, styled on their own apart from the motion design, and sit in one consistent place clear of faces and split lines. The episode title is written into the teleprompter script as a natural sentence near the start; when he says it, it animates as the episode's own title, like the intro of an episode, and the captions step aside for that line so the words appear once.

groups.title: Carousels: one clear point, ten cards at most
groups.statement: A carousel concretely teaches what its topic means in practice, backed by visuals, in ten cards at most unless the platform's native format allows more; its cards carry minimal text, no number in the top-left corner and no source list, which goes in the post description.

groups.title: A clean picture and seamless joins
groups.statement: Stable, well-framed footage with his head centred, untouched room treatment, and joins and transitions with no glitch, flash or doubled frame; a visual Critic checks before he sees it.

groups.title: Clean speech edits
groups.statement: Cut on true word boundaries checked by ear, keep picture and voice in sync, keep his natural ad-libs, and duck sniffs without cutting words.

groups.title: Every line clear on one hearing (adds to Words a stranger and a 12-year-old follow)
groups.statement: Every script, card and brief is clear on one read: each line is read aloud and smoothed before recording, every company or thing is named on first mention, every label and number is explained as it is heard, the precise term is used, an analogy stays whole, and pros and cons are plain; never a cryptic card, an ambiguous sentence, a vague pronoun or garbled shorthand.

groups.title: Composed frames
groups.statement: Every frame and card is laid out on a grid, filled with no dead space or cramped corners, aligned, and inside the safe area.

groups.title: Covers with the house's personality, for every crop
groups.statement: Covers and thumbnails are bold and on-brand, with plainly dressed people, drawn for each platform's real crop (wide and vertical), labelled by surface, and end cards designed into the reader's flow.

groups.title: Covers and first cards that stop the scroll (adds to Covers with the house's personality)
groups.statement: A cover, thumbnail or first card opens on a real-world photographic image or an engaging background, is built from a full designed template in the week's agreed theme, rotates the portrait, lets the headline take precedence and passes the house visual gate; never a text-only card, a face on plain black, the same portrait again, or extra logos and badges fighting the headline.

groups.title: Every element whole, apart, and filling the frame (adds to Composed frames)
groups.statement: Every animation, card, label and line of text sits fully inside the frame and its safe area, apart from every other element, and the frame is filled deliberately top to bottom; never a cropped animation, a clipped component, overlapping titles, large empty areas, visuals cramped into corners, or a vertical template with a third cut off.

groups.title: A fresh look for every piece
groups.statement: Each piece draws its look from the style bank and its own references; never reuse the last piece's layout, assets or portrait, or turn one liked reference into a house default.

groups.title: His face on camera, and clean joins (adds to A clean picture)
groups.statement: His eye line is corrected, his eyes are lit and visible, his face is never covered by split-screen panels or graphics, shots of him pan or zoom with intent, the Thursday cut keeps his face minimal beside Monday, Wednesday and Friday, and every join is frame-checked with no glitch or doubled frame.

groups.title: Scripts are his spoken words, with personality
groups.statement: A script is only the words he will say, in his natural joined phrasing, with dry wit and opinion, in a reflective tone, for the leader of a medium-sized company; no stage directions, no AI disclosure line.

groups.title: Honest, concrete titles
groups.statement: A title, cover or thumbnail makes a concrete claim that is in the piece and verified, in natural plain words a stranger cannot misread, framed fairly to every country, catchy enough to stop a scroll but never beyond what the piece shows. It names who did it, never 'they', 'it' or 'this' standing in for a name.

groups.title: The house brand on everything
groups.statement: Every asset and page carries the makeyourmindup wordmark and the brand book's fonts and colours, in premium, restrained chrome: one type family and one accent per day. Colour and energy come from real creative work and motion. Never toy-like, never muted or empty, never a plain black screen. On video the wordmark appears only at the close, never during the animated content; on a carousel, meme or Notes image it sits small in the bottom-right corner; a wide thumbnail carries none.

groups.title: The current intro and outro on every cut, exactly as designed
groups.statement: Every cut carries the current approved intro and outro for its weekday exactly as designed: an intro in colour and motion from the first frame, and the animated zooming outro with the real wordmark and 'follow for more'; a template that falls below recent work is retired at once.

groups.title: Licensed and sharp imagery
groups.statement: Use only licensed imagery with its source recorded, or original drawings, and never a soft or blurry picture.

groups.title: Every company's real logo, at equal size (adds to Real logos)
groups.statement: Every company discussed gets its own real, official logo on the cards or title plate, never a typed wordmark, a founder's name or a parent company's mark, and rival logos sit at the same visible scale in the same style.

groups.title: Motion that explains
groups.statement: Motion changes state to carry the argument, from the first frame; never static held stills with drawn arrows, never his face in every shot, never a stretch with no visual.

groups.title: Motion that is fast, full and always moving (adds to Motion that explains)
groups.statement: Motion design keeps moving across every panel, advances the narrative with real objects changing state, paces briskly and fills the frame, and text highlights finish cleanly in time with their words; never symbols that arrive and hold, a still with a couple of arrow circles, animation ten times too slow, or a typing effect.

groups.title: Always a music bed
groups.statement: A licensed bed runs under the whole cut, up under the intro and outro and low under his voice; never silence.

groups.title: Nothing on screen that carries no information
groups.statement: Every shape, mark, badge and icon on screen serves the point or a stated rule; never stray little abbreviations and marks, novelty badges like 'screwdriver included', decorative circles, or an icon that appears in some videos for no reason.

groups.title: Numbers as plain comparisons and clear verdicts
groups.statement: Turn every score into an everyday comparison and a plain win, lose or draw with counts; label charts with source, measure and scale; no pile of caveats.

groups.title: Words a stranger and a 12-year-old follow
groups.statement: Every line is read aloud before recording; every actor is named, every term explained, every analogy whole, and the reading age is 12.

groups.title: Made for each platform, clear of its buttons
groups.statement: Every post is designed for the platform and channel it appears on, with captions and on-screen elements inside that platform's safe area; never hidden beneath the app's buttons, usernames or caption bar, or cramped for the format.

groups.title: Committed predictions and fairly chosen examples (adds to Bold, checkable predictions)
groups.statement: No piece makes a prediction: no call, dated forecast, odds, confidence number or score (Krish, 2026-11-24: "get rid of everything that suggests predictions, calls, dated, etc etc"). Examples stay neutral, with Chinese flags or DeepSeek imagery only where the example is a Chinese AI.

groups.title: Real, dated evidence, never clipart
groups.statement: Show the real thing: dated screenshots, real products, real interactions and sourced charts; never clipart, emoji icons, stock gimmicks or a literal cartoon of a script analogy.

groups.title: Real logos, never stand-ins
groups.statement: Every company or product named gets its real, current logo, at equal visible size beside its rivals; never a typed name, a founder, a parent company or an outline box.

groups.title: Real, entertaining visuals for every point (adds to Real, dated evidence)
groups.statement: Every point is shown with the real thing: the actual advert, report or deck the voice names, live redacted screenshots of real interactions, real imagery blended with design in the brand's colours, real sample details on any diagram, a likeness that looks like the person, and a real visual held across each spoken analogy; never outline clipart, a generic robot, a screenshot of text as carousel imagery, a chart like old Excel, or a boring cut.

groups.title: Hook first, one story, one close
groups.statement: Open straight on a provocative hook (no preamble, no 'I'm Krish'), tell one story, use one opening and one closing screen, end on a spoken outro to the article, and keep each format to its length.

groups.title: Sharp pictures, and evidence big enough to read (adds to Licensed and sharp imagery)
groups.statement: Every picture is sharp, and every key screenshot or evidence card is sized so its text reads at normal viewing distance; never a soft first draft shipped as final, or evidence shrunk too small to read.

groups.title: A steady bed that fits the piece, and a treated voice (adds to Always a music bed)
groups.statement: The music runs one steady arc, loud at the open, soft and steady under speech, loud again at the close, with the opening bed fading out around 18 seconds into the next track, which stays audible; its tone matches the piece, and his voice is treated to sound deep, clear and professional; never volume rising and falling throughout, music burying the voice, dance music under a serious piece, or raw voice audio.

groups.title: Straight into the story, and a spoken close (adds to Hook first, one story, one close)
groups.statement: A script opens directly inside the story on a provocative hook, never by previewing its own parts or reciting facts, with a first frame that stays long enough to read; it tells one story start to finish, introduces every concept before using it, and ends on a spoken outro, never abruptly.

groups.title: Text set cleanly and premium (adds to Composed frames)
groups.statement: Card text is aligned precisely to the grid, centred on carousel story cards, reflowed so no single word sits alone on a line, and set in text and boxes that read as premium; never misaligned, off-centre, orphaned or cheap-looking.

groups.title: Titles that are concrete, true and impossible to misread (adds to Honest, concrete titles)
groups.statement: A title, cover line or headline states a concrete, specific claim or contrast, checked against the real facts, in words a stranger cannot misread about who did what or when, catchy enough to stop a scroll but never beyond what the piece shows. It names who did it: never "they", "it", "this" or another vague word standing in for a name. A collection is named for what is actually in it; never just a product name, a vague or inaccurate line, or a boring, amateur title.

groups.title: His natural voice, for a mid-sized company's leader (adds to Scripts are his spoken words)
groups.statement: Scripts use the natural phrasing, joins and asides he actually speaks, are written for the leader of a medium-sized company, and close in the same reflective, conversational voice as the rest; never clipped written sentences, a pitch to a small 'mum and dad' shop, or a bossy, preachy ending.

groups.title: Where the wordmark sits: small, and clear of the action
groups.statement: The wordmark stays off the main animated content and off vertical video templates and belongs on the closing outro card; it sits small and subtle in a bottom corner on carousels and bottom right under a meme, and no animation ever crosses it.

groups.title: On-screen words add, never repeat
groups.statement: On-screen words add a source, date, number or picture the voice doesn't give, read in about a second, and sit beside a real image; never a text-only card, never a copy of the captions. The one exception is the episode title moment: when he says the episode title, it animates as its own title and the captions step aside for that line, so the words appear once.

groups.title: On-screen words add, match their picture and label truly (adds to On-screen words add)
groups.statement: On-screen words add a source, date, exact number or name the voice does not say, or give way to a simple picture a layperson grasps in three seconds; each card's quote matches its image, each eyebrow names its own segment, and nothing carries a value-free label like 'Krish's take' or 'illustrative'.
